transcription_notes: SOURCE/LAYOUT: Cambridge UL MS Add. 1570, crop Samuel01.jpg ONLY. Page = 3 columns, dense Ethiopic (Ge'ez) book hand with red rubrication; reading order is top-to-bottom within a column, then next column left-to-right. Image is ~1129x1441 px for the WHOLE 3-column folio (~0.6 MP) -> very low effective resolution per glyph; I cropped each column into tall bands and upscaled 6.5-8x with autocontrast to read. CH.1 EXTENT: A multi-line RED rubricated heading occupies the top of column 1 (incipit 'In the name of the merciful and compassionate God... I write the Book of Reigns of Israel and Judah...' ending with red 'ክፍል ፩' = Part 1) -- this heading is NOT verse text and is excluded. Ch.1 running text begins column 1 ~line 8 with 'ወሀሎ ፩ ብእሲ እምነ አርማቴም' (1:1), fills the rest of column 1 (through ~v.11 partial), continues down the WHOLE of column 2 (v.11 cont. through v.28 partial), and ends on the FIRST (red) line of column 3 with the last words of v.28 ('...ወሰገደ ህየ ለእግዚአብሔር ምስለ ኤሊ'). CH.1->CH.2 BOUNDARY: Chapter 2 (Hannah's Song, 'My heart is established/exults in the LORD...') begins on the SECOND line of column 3 of Samuel01.jpg; I stopped there. line_start values are best estimates of the line WITHIN the stated column (column 1's chapter text starts ~line 8 because of the heading; columns 2 and 3 line numbers count from the column top). SEGMENTATION: the manuscript has NO numbered verses; segmentation into 28 verses is MY best judgement from red rubric ornaments/letters, the '፡' word-divider, and narrative sense, aligned to the conventional Hannah-narrative structure -- it is NOT a count forced from memory; verse boundaries (esp. vv.4-6, 22-25) are genuinely ambiguous and could shift by a clause. NUMERAL RULE: the canonical numeral-tokenization rule was applied -- every Ethiopic numeral glyph (e.g. ፩ ፪ ፲) is its own standalone token in the tokens[] array, never glued to letters; numerals are kept adjacent only inside the human-readable geez string. HONESTY / LEGIBILITY (critical): This hand at THIS crop resolution is only PARTIALLY legible. Reliably readable: red rubricated words, the recurring divine name እግዚአብሔር, frequent proper names (ሕልቃና/ሐና/ኤሊ/ሳሙኤል/አርማቴም/ሴሎ), structural particles, and the CONSONANT SKELETON of most words. NOT reliably resolved: the vowel-order diacritics that distinguish the 7 Ethiopic orders (ሀ/ሁ/ሂ/ሃ/ህ/ሄ/ህ/ሆ) on a large share of glyphs, plus several near-homograph base forms (በ/ነ/ተ, ቀ/ቐ, ጠ/ጰ, ሰ/ሠ, ሐ/ሓ/ኀ). Consequently the geez/tokens reflect my single best per-word reading but the per-glyph (esp. vowel-order) fidelity is LOW; ~35-45% of tokens are flagged uncertain and they do NOT cluster only on physically damaged spots -- the uncertainty is pervasive and driven mainly by global downscaling blur, with additional 'damaged' spots where ink bleed-through/smudge sits over specific glyphs (v.5 area especially). Genuinely unreadable stretches were marked with the literal ⟦illegible⟧ sentinel (vv.5,11,18,22,24,25) rather than reconstructed; NO word was filled or corrected from memory of the known Biblical text. SUBJECTIVE READ: I could recover the narrative shape and most word skeletons with reasonable confidence, but a strict verbatim glyph-exact transcription (diacritic level) is NOT achievable from this single low-res crop -- a meaningful fraction of the fine reading is best-effort, not certain. Higher-resolution images (the GG-00106 ~5MP scans referenced elsewhere) would be needed for a defensible critical-edition transcription.
